clue.text: Promoter of change, one leaving country in company of actors

indicators.note: in places the shortened country inside the company of actors

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors in a play

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for one walks out of the country's name

parts.note: Italy is the country
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A travelling actor quits a country's touring troupe, prompting change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promoter of change' reads like a reformer, but it is the chemistry term; 'one' is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry and in everyday speech, a catalyst is something that triggers or speeds change.

clue.text: Precipitate downfall of brash hangers-on in court

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the court's letters

parts.note: brash means loud
burs are prickly seeds that cling, hangers-on

explanation.surface: Loud hangers-on at court cause a sudden fall from power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precipitate downfall' looks like a political collapse; it is a sudden heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudburst is a sudden torrential fall of rain, a downfall of precipitation.

clue.text: Small child's drink

explanation.surface: A little one's beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a young child and a small dram of liquor.

clue.text: Old metalworker alternatively employed in seagoing vessel

indicators.note: employed in puts the word for alternatively inside the ship

parts.note: a liner is an ocean ship
or means alternatively

explanation.surface: An old craftsman found work aboard a ship instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A loriner was a maker of bits, spurs and other metal fittings for horses' harness.

clue.text: Police officer, one demanding payment for engine booster

parts.note: super is short for superintendent
someone who charges is a charger

explanation.surface: A police officer bills for an engine part.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercharger forces extra air into an engine to raise its power, a booster.

clue.text: When speaking, caught sight of a predator

indicators.note: When speaking says the words are to be heard said out loud, not read

parts.note: caught sight of a means spied a

explanation.surface: Someone tells of glimpsing a hunting animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'spied a' runs together into the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders trap and eat insects, so they are hunters of other creatures.

clue.text: Stars secure as you and me?

parts.note: to peg is to secure
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: Can celebrities be pinned down as ordinary people like us?
explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus is a constellation of the northern sky, a group of stars.

clue.text: Old battleship from Aden at sea in dry period

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the dry spell

parts.note: a drought is a long dry spell

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of Aden are mixed

explanation.surface: An old warship sailed from Aden during a dry spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the naval surface but is the anagram signal; 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Dreadnought gave its name to a class of big-gun battleships of the early 1900s.

clue.text: Baby food from river, one in South Wales

parts.note: the Usk is a river, one in South Wales

explanation.surface: Infant food produced near a Welsh river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'river': the Usk flows through South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusk is a hard dry biscuit given to teething infants.

clue.text: Sacked constables gathered round first of remote rock formations

parts.note: someone sacked is out of a job

indicators.note: the constables are gathered round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: police constables are cops

indicators.note: first of selects the opening letter of remote

explanation.surface: Dismissed police officers cluster around a distant geological feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered round' puts R, the first of 'remote', inside COPS.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is a mass of bedrock exposed above the soil, a kind of rock formation.

clue.text: Monstrous female knocked back game on ship

indicators.note: knocked back means the game's name is turned to read backwards

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game
re means on, concerning
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman downs a drink and plays a game aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ogre, a monster of fairy tales, is the feminine form of the word.

clue.text: Musician caught by Liberal painter digesting popular film

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: digesting means the painter takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: a painter is an artist
in means popular
ET is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A musician arrested by a Liberal artist absorbed in a hit movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like an arrest, but it is the cricket scorecard abbreviation; 'popular' and 'film' together sit inside the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinettist plays the clarinet, so is a musician.

clue.text: Dispersed, as licensed trade could be

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the two words might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub trade spread across many places, as the licensing trade might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Decentralised power or industry is spread out from one centre, so dispersed.

clue.text: Narrow American abandoning stock covered by agreement

parts.note: to narrow is to contract

indicators.note: abandoning means the American letters leave the word for stock

parts.note: a stock phrase is the usual one

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded American quits stock dealing under a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes US out of USUAL, leaving UAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contractual is bound by or arising from a contract, a formal agreement.

clue.text: Old woman in dam near barking dog

indicators.note: in puts the old woman inside the dam

parts.note: a weir is a small dam on a river
ma is mother, an old woman

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of near are scrambled

explanation.surface: A mother near a dam hears a dog barking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weimaraner is a grey German hunting breed of dog.

clue.text: Partly useful — narrow like some bones

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some bones are described as partly useful and narrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is a forearm bone, and the adjective describes things relating to it.

clue.text: Dread voiced? Manage to accept conclusion of this forecast

indicators.note: to accept means the pair takes the final letter inside them
voiced says the word for dread is heard said aloud, not spelt

parts.note: dread means horror
to manage is to cope

indicators.note: conclusion of picks the last letter of the word this

explanation.surface: Fearing what lies ahead, someone braces to accept how this prediction ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound-alike for dread is rough: the first part is heard as a clipped 'horror'; the final S of 'this' sits between the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrological reading of the stars predicts a person's future, a forecast.

clue.text: Waste material produced by club after fight

indicators.note: after places the club's word behind the fight's word

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Rubbish is made by a club after a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded metal for melting down is scrap, a form of waste material.

clue.text: Game taking place over in borders of Pakistan

indicators.note: in puts the pieces inside those outer letters
borders of picks the outer letters of Pakistan

parts.note: on means happening, taking place
too means over, excessively

explanation.surface: A game happening again in Pakistan's frontier regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon is a card game, the British name for twenty-one or blackjack.

clue.text: Stick used by extremely brittle Muslim prince's widow

indicators.note: used by sets the stick after the end letters, which take it up
extremely picks the two extreme letters of brittle

parts.note: gum is glue, something that sticks

explanation.surface: Glue is used on something extremely fragile.
explanation.definitionFit: Begum is a title for a Muslim woman of high rank, especially a prince's widow.

clue.text: Little creature regularly baited around Orient

indicators.note: around means the picked letters sit around the Orient's word
regularly picks every other letter of baited

parts.note: the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: A small animal is lured with bait around the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the odd letters of 'baited', and those letters wrap round the compass point the Orient names.
explanation.definitionFit: Beastie is a Scottish and playful word for a small animal or insect.

clue.text: Overseas leader's note misinterpreted race's torment

parts.note: C is a musical note

indicators.note: misinterpreted says the letters of the next words are read wrongly, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A message was misread as describing a race's suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overseas' means American usage: in the US the lead violinist of an orchestra has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: In American orchestras the principal first violin, who leads the orchestra, holds this title.

clue.text: Book theatre turns

definitions.meaning: the ... of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Reserve seats for the stage performances.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Bible book and also the separate items on a variety bill.

clue.text: Voucher scam taking in publisher

indicators.note: taking in means the scam's word encloses the publisher

parts.note: a con is a scam
OUP is Oxford University Press, a publisher

explanation.surface: A discount voucher turns out to be a fraud that fools a publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' also means fooling, which is the surface sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a slip giving a discount or entitlement, a voucher.

clue.text: Sports contest initially banned in most of Leinster town

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of banned and in
most of drops the last letter

parts.note: Athlone is a town in Leinster, Ireland

explanation.surface: A sports event was banned in most of an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' covers both 'banned' and 'in'; 'most of' cuts ATHLONE to ATHLON.
explanation.definitionFit: A biathlon is a sporting event combining two disciplines, usually skiing and shooting.

clue.text: Scottish smoker cross about being abandoned by English

indicators.note: about turns what remains to read backwards
being abandoned by means the English letter leaves the cross

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: An angry Scot who smokes is deserted by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being abandoned by' drops E from MULE, giving MUL; 'about' turns that round. 'Smoker' is a chimney here.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a lum is a chimney, which smokes, hence a smoker.

clue.text: Isotonic solution chap brought into function

indicators.note: brought into puts the chap inside the function

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
Al is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man is drafted into a role involving a medical drip.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltwater drip matching the body's salt level is the standard isotonic fluid.

clue.text: King trapped in vessel leads to banner headline

indicators.note: trapped in puts the king inside the vessel

parts.note: a steamer is a ship, a vessel
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A king stuck aboard ship makes front-page news.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a headline running across a full newspaper page, like a banner.
